scenario_stem:
Coral Ridge Hotel is a 4-star resort in a coastal tourist town in Country X, operating 120 guest rooms and 3 restaurants. The hotel employs 95 staff, of whom 60 are full-time and 35 are part-time. The head chef, who was paid $54,000 a year, resigned after 6 years. The general manager must decide whether to promote Marco, a section chef on $42,000 a year with 5 years' service, or recruit externally.

Marco knows the kitchen brigade and the summer menu but has never run a whole kitchen. The hotel placed a job advertisement in the regional newspaper costing $350 and received 24 applications within 2 weeks. Of these, 9 came from existing staff and 15 from outside the hotel. The advertised salary for the new head chef is $55,000 a year. The summer season lasts 14 weeks, with occupancy averaging 90%, and the wage bill already totals $2.4 million a year.

questions.question_text: Define 'external recruitment'.
questions.model_answer: External recruitment is the process of hiring new workers from outside the business, for example through job advertisements, instead of promoting existing employees. [2]

knowledge_max_2: Hiring new workers from outside the business
Attracting outside candidates, for example through job advertisements, rather than promoting existing staff

questions.question_text: Explain two reasons why Coral Ridge Hotel placed a job advertisement in the regional newspaper.
questions.model_answer: Placing a job advertisement informs potential candidates outside the hotel about the head chef vacancy, widening the pool beyond the 9 internal applicants [k]. Advertising at a cost of $350 attracted 15 external applications within 2 weeks, giving the manager a wider choice of experienced chefs [app]. An advertisement can set out the salary and the requirements of the role [k], which filters for candidates willing to lead 3 restaurants at the advertised salary of $55,000 a year [app].

knowledge_max_2: The advert informs potential candidates that a vacancy exists, widening the applicant pool
The advert sets out the salary and requirements, attracting suitable applicants and filtering out unsuitable ones
application_max_2: The advert cost $350 and attracted 15 external applications within 2 weeks
$55,000 salary is advertised for managing 3 restaurants

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits to Coral Ridge Hotel of promoting Marco to head chef.
questions.model_answer: Promoting Marco is cheaper and quicker than external recruitment [k], because the hotel avoids the $350 advertising cost and the time spent interviewing unknown applicants [app], so the new head chef can be in post before the 14-week summer season and the wage bill of $2.4 million is not strained further [an]. Internal promotion also rewards loyalty and motivates other staff [k]. Marco has 5 years' service and knows the kitchen brigade and the summer menu, so service can continue smoothly across the 3 restaurants [app]. Because guests will find familiar quality during a season when occupancy averages 90%, reviews and repeat bookings are more likely to hold up [an].

knowledge_max_2: Internal promotion is cheaper and quicker than external recruitment
Promoting internally rewards and motivates loyal existing staff
application_max_2: $350 advertising avoided; Marco has 5 years' service
Marco knows the kitchen brigade and the summer menu across the 3 restaurants
analysis_max_2: Head chef in post before the 14-week peak, avoiding disruption at high occupancy
Continuity of quality protects reputation, reviews and revenue during the 90% occupancy season

questions.question_text: Do you think Coral Ridge Hotel should promote Marco or recruit a new head chef externally? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Promoting Marco is cheaper and faster [k]. Marco has 5 years' service, knows the kitchen brigade and the summer menu, and the promotion costs about $13,000 a year more ($55,000 minus $42,000) rather than $350 of advertising plus weeks of interviews [app]. Staying with Marco protects food quality and cover during the 14-week peak when occupancy averages 90% [an]. However, Marco has never run a whole kitchen, and external candidates may bring broader experience across several kitchens and fresh menu ideas [k]. The 15 external applications include chefs prepared to accept $55,000; a stronger outsider could lift standards and motivate the brigade across the 3 restaurants [app]. An external hire might also introduce new routines that improve standards, but risks upsetting established staff and losing continuity during the busiest season [an]. Overall, the hotel should promote Marco because the risk and cost of external hiring so close to the 14-week season are too high, and his 5 years here make him the safest pair of hands [eval]. If the board wanted a long-term transformation of the menu, an external search after the summer would be wiser, but this vacancy must be filled immediately [eval].

knowledge_max_2: Internal promotion: cheaper, faster, known candidate, motivates staff
External recruitment: wider pool, fresh skills/experience, but costlier and riskier
application_max_2: Marco: 5 years' service; knows brigade and menu; promotion costs about $13,000 a year more
15 external applications; $55,000 salary; 90% occupancy; 14-week season
analysis_max_2: Internal pick protects quality and continuity during peak season
External pick could raise standards but disrupt staff and delay the start date
evaluation_max_2: Clear overall judgement justified by timing, cost and risk
Recognises when external recruitment would become the better option

scenario_stem:
BrightPath Logistics runs a parcel distribution depot in Country X, employing 78 staff: 50 full-time drivers and warehouse operatives earning $15 an hour, and 28 part-time workers earning $12 an hour. Parcel volumes rise by 45% during the 10-week pre-Christmas peak, when the depot handles 9,600 parcels a week. Last year, 140 parcels were damaged and 12 were lost because staff were overstretched.

The operations manager must choose between hiring 20 additional part-time workers for the peak only or 10 additional full-time staff all year on a salary of $31,200. Part-time workers are paid only for hours worked but cannot drive heavy vehicles or operate the new forklifts. Full-time staff receive 6 weeks of training and would stay after the peak ends. The recruitment budget is $4,000 and advertising costs $180 per vacancy. The depot expects similar volumes next peak season.

questions.question_text: Define 'part-time employment'.
questions.model_answer: Part-time employment is a job in which the employee works fewer hours per week than a full-time employee, often on flexible or reduced shifts, and is paid for the hours worked. [2]

knowledge_max_2: Works fewer hours per week than a full-time employee
Paid for the hours worked, often on flexible or reduced shifts

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages to BrightPath Logistics of hiring 20 additional part-time workers for the peak.
questions.model_answer: Part-time workers are paid only for the hours they work [k], so during the 10-week pre-Christmas peak, when volumes rise by 45% to 9,600 parcels a week, the depot pays extra wages only when the extra capacity is actually needed [app]. Additional part-time staff reduce the overload on the existing 78 staff [k], helping to prevent repeats of the 140 damaged and 12 lost parcels that occurred last year [app].

knowledge_max_2: Pay only for the hours worked; labour cost flexes with demand
Extra staff relieve pressure and reduce errors/losses
application_max_2: 10-week peak; volumes rise 45% to 9,600 parcels a week; $12 an hour
140 damaged and 12 lost parcels last year; 78 existing staff

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages of employing 10 additional full-time staff all year.
questions.model_answer: Full-time staff can be trained and trusted with demanding tasks [k]. The 50 current full-time drivers and operatives already handle heavy vehicles and forklifts, and new full-time hires would receive 6 weeks of training [app], widening the pool of skilled staff available all year, not just in December [an]. Full-time staff remain after the peak, giving the depot stable capacity [k]. Ten full-time salaries cost $312,000 a year (10 x $31,200), but these staff can cover quieter months and stand in for absences [app], reducing reliance on agency cover and repeated seasonal recruitment every December [an].

knowledge_max_2: Full-time staff can receive full training and handle more demanding tasks
Full-time staff provide year-round stable capacity and continuity
application_max_2: 6 weeks of training; heavy vehicles and forklifts; 50 current full-time staff
10 x $31,200 = $312,000 a year; stays after the peak ends
analysis_max_2: Wider skilled pool all year reduces bottlenecks and dependence on December cover
Year-round presence lowers agency costs and re-recruitment effort

questions.question_text: Do you think BrightPath Logistics should hire 20 additional part-time workers for the peak or 10 additional full-time staff all year? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Hiring 20 part-time workers is cheaper and more flexible [k]. At $12 an hour part-timers cost less than the $15 full-time rate and are paid only for hours worked, and 20 vacancies at $180 each total $3,600, still inside the $4,000 recruitment budget [app]. Bringing in extra hands should stop the 140 damaged and 12 lost parcels that overstretched staff caused last year [an]. However, part-time staff cannot drive heavy vehicles or operate forklifts [k], so the depot would still rely on its 50 full-time staff for the hardest tasks and might repeat the same overload in January returns or other peaks [app]. Full-time hires at $31,200 each would stay year-round, receive 6 weeks of training and cut the need to re-recruit every December [an]. Overall, the depot should hire the 20 part-time peak workers because demand is temporary and $312,000 of annual salary for year-round cover is hard to justify for a peak that lasts 10 weeks [eval]. If volumes stayed high all year, or forklift-certified full-time staff were urgently needed, the full-time option would become worth the extra cost [eval].

knowledge_max_2: Part-time: flexible, cheaper per hour, suits short peaks
Full-time: permanent, trained, versatile but costly year-round
application_max_2: $12 vs $15 an hour; $180 per vacancy; 20 vacancies = $3,600 inside $4,000 budget
10 x $31,200 = $312,000; 10-week peak; 9,600 parcels; 140 damaged and 12 lost
analysis_max_2: Cheap flexible capacity matched to a known 10-week peak reduces overload and parcel losses
Full-time gives year-round skill and stability but overspends for a temporary need
evaluation_max_2: Clear overall judgement justified by the temporary nature of the peak and the cost arithmetic
Recognises the circumstances in which the full-time option would be preferable

scenario_stem:
Meadowbrook Day Nursery is a private nursery in Country X caring for 48 children aged 2 to 5 years. It is staffed by 14 people: 9 full-time practitioners earning $26,000 a year and 5 part-time assistants working 15 hours a week. One full-time practitioner has resigned and the owner must choose a replacement before the autumn term. The vacancy was advertised at $250 and attracted 30 applications within 3 weeks.

Of these applications, 18 enclosed a curriculum vitae (CV) and 12 completed the nursery's application form, which asks 8 standard questions about qualifications, experience and childcare training. CVs vary widely in layout and detail, making comparison slow, while the forms give consistent information. However, the forms reveal less about personality. Interview panels cost $120 per candidate in staff time and the total recruitment budget for this role is $800.

questions.question_text: Define 'application form'.
questions.model_answer: An application form is a standard document produced by the business that applicants complete to provide details such as personal information, qualifications and experience, allowing the employer to compare candidates fairly. [2]

knowledge_max_2: Standard document produced by the employer for applicants to complete
Gathers consistent information (qualifications, experience, personal details) to aid fair comparison

questions.question_text: Explain two reasons why Meadowbrook Day Nursery might prefer the application forms when shortlisting.
questions.model_answer: Application forms present every candidate's information in the same format [k]. With 30 applications received in 3 weeks, the owner can scan the 12 completed forms quickly against the 8 standard questions instead of comparing 18 different CV layouts [app]. Forms ensure the nursery gets the specific information it needs [k]. The form's questions on qualifications, experience and childcare training directly test whether applicants meet the requirements for caring for children aged 2 to 5 [app].

knowledge_max_2: Forms give a consistent, directly comparable format
Forms gather specific job-relevant information the employer chooses
application_max_2: 30 applications in 3 weeks; 12 forms versus 18 CVs; 8 standard questions
Qualifications, experience and childcare training questions; children aged 2 to 5

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages of inviting shortlisted candidates for an interview.
questions.model_answer: Interviews let the owner probe claims made on the forms or CVs [k]. With $120 of staff time per candidate and a total budget of $800 (minus $250 already spent on the advertisement), the nursery can interview only the strongest candidates and check their claims face to face [app], which reduces the risk of hiring unsuitable staff for the 48 children [an]. Interviews also give candidates the chance to ask questions about the role [k]. Discussing the $26,000 full-time salary, the 9 existing full-time practitioners and daily duties helps both sides judge fit before the autumn term [app], lowering the chance of an early resignation and the $120 per-interview cost being wasted [an].

knowledge_max_2: Interviews verify/probe candidate claims and reveal interpersonal qualities
Interviews allow two-way communication; candidates can ask questions and judge fit
application_max_2: $120 per candidate; $800 budget; $250 spent on the advertisement
$26,000 salary; 9 full-time colleagues; autumn term deadline
analysis_max_2: Better screening reduces risk of unsuitable hires around young children
Two-way fit assessment lowers early turnover and wasted recruitment spend

questions.question_text: Do you think Meadowbrook Day Nursery should shortlist using the CVs or the application forms? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Application forms give consistent information the nursery can compare quickly [k]. The 12 completed forms answer the 8 standard questions directly, so the owner can shortlist confidently before paying $120 per interview from the remaining budget [app]. This reduces the risk of hiring someone unsuitable to work with the 48 children aged 2 to 5 [an]. However, CVs reveal more about personality, motivation and experiences such as first-aid courses, and the 18 CVs received may contain stronger candidates than the forms show [k]. A detailed CV might reveal qualities the standard form cannot capture, and rejecting them all could leave the nursery choosing only from the form-fillers [app]. Over-reliance on the form alone could cause the nursery to miss the most enthusiastic applicant for the role [an]. Overall, the nursery should shortlist using the application forms because consistency and the 8 targeted questions suit a safeguarding-critical childcare role, and the budget does not stretch to interviewing widely from an unverified CV pool [eval]. If strong candidates emerge on the forms, CVs can be read as supporting evidence, but the form should remain the primary tool [eval].

knowledge_max_2: Application forms: consistent, comparable, fast to process
CVs: richer picture of personality/motivation, but variable layout and detail
application_max_2: 12 completed forms vs 18 CVs; 8 standard questions; $120 per interview; $800 budget
48 children aged 2 to 5; children need safe, vetted carers; autumn term deadline
analysis_max_2: Forms speed shortlisting and cut the risk of unsuitable hires in a care setting
CVs may hide stronger candidates; form-only shortlisting risks lower quality of hire
evaluation_max_2: Reasoned overall judgement anchored to budget, safeguarding and comparability
Acknowledges the CV's value as secondary evidence

scenario_stem:
Tekworks Electronics repairs and assembles computers and tablets at 2 workshops in Country X, employing 64 people. It produces 1,100 repaired devices a month at an average price of $190. The business has won a new client and must open an assembly line, requiring 12 electronics assemblers within 6 weeks.

The HR manager must choose between a practical assessment (soldering and fault-finding, 2 hours, $45 per candidate) and a 30-minute panel interview costing $25 per candidate; running both costs $70 per applicant. The assembly line must reach 400 units a month within 4 months, with at least 98% fault-free units. The recruitment budget is $3,000 and 55 people have applied so far. The manager plans to invite 35 applicants to the next stage and hopes to have the full team in place before the first client shipment.

questions.question_text: Define 'interview' in the context of selection.
questions.model_answer: An interview is a face-to-face meeting between a job applicant and the business, used to assess the applicant's suitability, skills and attitude for the role. [2]

knowledge_max_2: Face-to-face (or video) meeting between applicant and employer
Used to assess suitability, skills and attitude for the role

questions.question_text: Explain two reasons why Tekworks Electronics should test the 12 assemblers before hiring them.
questions.model_answer: Testing reveals the practical ability that an interview cannot show [k]. The assembly line needs soldering and fault-finding skill, so a $45 practical assessment shows exactly which of the 35 invited applicants can meet the 98% fault-free requirement [app]. Testing reduces the risk of costly mistakes and rework [k]. With the line due to reach 400 units a month within 4 months, hiring untested assemblers risks faulty devices and a damaged relationship with the new client [app].

knowledge_max_2: Tests measure actual job skills directly rather than claimed ability
Testing identifies unsuitable candidates and reduces hiring errors and rework
application_max_2: Soldering and fault-finding; 98% fault-free requirement
35 invited applicants; $45 assessment; 400 units a month within 4 months

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits of using interviews as part of the selection process.
questions.model_answer: Interviews let the panel assess communication and teamwork [k], so the manager can check how applicants would fit into the team of 64 across the 2 workshops before devices priced at $190 are entrusted to them [app], improving team fit and reducing early turnover [an]. Interviews also let candidates ask about the job [k], so shortlisted applicants can understand the 400-unit monthly target, the 6-week hiring deadline and working patterns [app], meaning expectations match reality and the $3,000 recruitment budget is not wasted on someone who resigns quickly [an].

knowledge_max_2: Interviews assess communication, attitude and team fit
Interviews let candidates ask questions and form realistic expectations
application_max_2: Devices priced at $190; team of 64 across 2 workshops
400-unit monthly target; 6-week deadline; $3,000 budget
analysis_max_2: Better fit reduces turnover and disruption in the new line
Realistic expectations reduce early resignations, saving recruitment cost

questions.question_text: Do you think Tekworks Electronics should use practical assessments or panel interviews to select the 12 assemblers? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Practical assessments directly measure the exact skills the assembly line needs [k]. A $45 assessment for 35 applicants costs $1,575, leaving $1,425 of the $3,000 budget, and shows who can actually solder to the 98% fault-free standard [app]. Choosing by observed skill rather than talk minimises rework and protects delivery of 400 units a month within 4 months [an]. However, practical tests alone cannot show how candidates communicate under pressure or fit into the 64-person team [k]. The $25 interview would reveal reliability and willingness to start within 6 weeks; running both costs $70 per applicant, or $2,450 for 35, still within budget [app]. A brilliant solderer who quits after a week would leave the line short-staffed and waste selection time [an]. Overall, practical assessments are the essential tool because the role is skill-critical and the client's 98% fault-free clause leaves no margin for unsuitable technicians [eval]. Interviews should be added only as a brief final check for the chosen 12, not as the main basis of selection [eval].

knowledge_max_2: Practical tests show real soldering/fault-finding competence
Interviews assess communication, reliability and team fit
application_max_2: $45 x 35 = $1,575; $3,000 budget; $70 per applicant combined; 98% fault-free
400 units a month; 4 months; 6-week start; 2 workshops of 64 people
analysis_max_2: Test-first selection minimises rework and quality failure for the new client
Interview-only selection risks hiring polished speakers who cannot solder
evaluation_max_2: Clear judgement: practical assessments are essential, interviews secondary
Notes that running both still fits the $3,000 budget

scenario_stem:
Sunfield Care Home is a residential care home in Country X providing 60 places for elderly residents. It is staffed by 38 full-time carers earning $13.50 an hour and 12 part-time night staff. The senior care supervisor, who retires soon, coordinates rotas for 50 staff, reviews care plans and keeps medication records up to date.

The home has a recruitment budget of $650. One candidate is Priya, a senior carer earning $14.25 an hour with 7 years at the home and all leadership training completed; she would accept promotion at $15.50 an hour. The alternative is an external advertisement costing $300, likely to attract applicants, some holding nursing qualifications. Resident occupancy is 93%. Last year an unsuitable external hire resigned within 4 months, costing $2,100 in agency cover and another advertisement. The manager wants continuity of care for the 60 residents.

questions.question_text: Define 'recruitment'.
questions.model_answer: Recruitment is the process of identifying that a business needs a new employee, attracting suitable candidates and filling the vacancy. [2]

knowledge_max_2: Identifying the need for a new employee / a vacancy
Attracting and selecting a suitable candidate to fill it

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages of recruiting the senior care supervisor internally.
questions.model_answer: Internal recruitment is cheaper and quicker [k]. The home avoids the external $300 advertising cost and weeks of interviews, staying within its $650 budget while keeping the rota fully covered [app]. The internal candidate is a known quantity [k]. Priya has 7 years at Sunfield and has completed all leadership training, so the manager can predict her reliability and medication-record accuracy at 93% occupancy across the 60 places [app].

knowledge_max_2: Internal recruitment is cheaper and quicker; no external advertising cost
Internal candidates are known to the business, so performance and reliability can be predicted
application_max_2: $300 advertising avoided; $650 budget respected; $14.25 current pay
Priya: 7 years, all leadership training done; 93% occupancy; 60 places

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages of recruiting the senior care supervisor externally.
questions.model_answer: External recruitment brings skills the home currently lacks [k]. Some applicants may hold nursing qualifications, adding clinical oversight that neither Priya nor the other carers can offer today [app], which could raise care standards across the home's 60 places [an]. A wider choice of candidates [k]. A $300 advertisement could attract hundreds of applications, giving the manager genuine choice rather than relying on a single internal candidate [app], which increases the chance of appointing a strong leader able to cut the agency costs that hit $2,100 last year [an].

knowledge_max_2: External recruitment brings in new skills/qualifications not held internally
External recruitment widens the applicant pool and gives genuine choice
application_max_2: Possible nursing-qualified applicants; $300 advertisement
$2,100 agency cover spent last year after a weak hire; 60 places
analysis_max_2: Added clinical oversight could lift standards of care for all residents
Wider pool raises the odds of a stronger appointment and lower agency spend

questions.question_text: Do you think Sunfield Care Home should promote Priya or recruit a senior care supervisor externally? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Promoting Priya is cheaper, safer and immediate [k]. She has 7 years at the home and all leadership training, asking only $15.50 an hour instead of $14.25 ($1.25 more, about $2,600 a year for 2,080 full-time hours), versus $300 of external advertising plus the risk of another failure like last year's $2,100 agency cover bill [app]. Appointing Priya keeps continuity of care at 93% occupancy, protects rota planning for 50 staff and rewards loyalty [an]. However, promoting internally excludes outsiders with nursing qualifications who could lift clinical oversight and challenge stale routines [k]. External advertising attracts a far wider field, and the strongest candidate might improve medication records, care planning and morale beyond Priya's level [app]. If Priya's promotion simply re-shuffles existing problems rather than solving them, the home could be worse off within months [an]. Overall, the home should promote Priya because she is known, trained, immediately available and far cheaper than another external failure, which matters most at 93% occupancy with vulnerable residents [eval]. An external search after the budget recovers, or next time a clinical skill gap appears, would be the sensible way to add outside expertise later [eval].

knowledge_max_2: Internal: cheaper, immediate, known, motivates staff
External: fresh skills and wider pool, but higher risk and cost
application_max_2: Priya: 7 years, all training done; $14.25 to $15.50 ($1.25 more, about $2,600 a year)
$300 external advertising; $2,100 spent last year; 93% occupancy; rotas for 50 staff
analysis_max_2: Continuity protects resident care and avoids disruption while the vacancy is open
External hire could add nursing skills but risks another costly mis-hire
evaluation_max_2: Clear justified recommendation tied to continuity, cost and risk
Identifies when external recruitment would become the better option

scenario_stem:
Riverview Leisure Centre is a public leisure facility in Country X with 2 swimming pools, a gym and a sports hall, employing 40 full-time staff. Attendances rose 18% last year to 210,000 visits, so opening hours increased to 14 hours a day, 7 days a week.

The manager must decide between recruiting 8 part-time lifeguards to cover the new evening and weekend sessions at $11.50 an hour, or 4 full-time lifeguards on $24,500 a year. Full-time lifeguards would also open and close the pools and complete gym induction checks. Part-time staff can supervise only 1 pool each and work 30-minute shifts. Full-time contracts include 5 weeks of annual leave. The recruitment budget is $900, of which $280 would be spent on advertising. The centre wants the new staff in place before the summer holidays begin.

questions.question_text: Define 'full-time employment'.
questions.model_answer: Full-time employment is a job in which the employee works the standard number of hours each week set by the employer, usually around 35 to 40 hours, on an ongoing basis. [2]

knowledge_max_2: Works the full/standard working week (about 35-40 hours)
On an ongoing, usually permanent basis for the business

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages of hiring 8 part-time lifeguards for the evening and weekend sessions.
questions.model_answer: Part-time cover matches staffing to demand [k], so the new 14-hour days can be covered at $11.50 an hour only when pools are busy, instead of paying $24,500 salaries all year [app]. Eight part-time lifeguards provide scheduling flexibility [k], covering 30-minute shifts and just 1 pool each across 2 pools, and they can cover for one another at short notice [app].

knowledge_max_2: Pay only for the hours needed; labour cost matches demand
Flexible shifts and more staff provide cover and resilience
application_max_2: $11.50 an hour; 14-hour days; evenings and weekends
1 pool each; 30-minute shifts; 2 pools; $24,500 full-time alternative

questions.question_text: Explain two advantages of hiring 4 full-time lifeguards instead.
questions.model_answer: Full-time lifeguards can take on wider duties [k]. They would open and close the pools and complete gym induction checks, tasks that part-timers on 30-minute shifts cannot practically handle [app], giving consistent standards at both ends of the 14-hour day [an]. Four full-time staff are also easier to train and supervise than 8 part-timers [k]. At $24,500 each, totalling $98,000 a year, they receive 5 weeks of annual leave arranged around demand and stay year-round [app], which lowers induction and turnover costs and strengthens safety compliance [an].

knowledge_max_2: Full-time staff take on wider, end-to-end duties
Fewer staff are easier to train, supervise and retain
application_max_2: Open and close duties; gym induction checks; 30-minute shifts impractical
$24,500 each, $98,000 total; 5 weeks annual leave; 14-hour day
analysis_max_2: End-of-day cover improves pool safety and consistent standards
Lower turnover and training burden; stronger safety compliance

questions.question_text: Do you think Riverview Leisure Centre should hire 8 part-time lifeguards or 4 full-time lifeguards? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Hiring 8 part-time lifeguards costs less and flexes with demand [k]. At $11.50 an hour, covering only evenings and weekends is cheaper than $98,000 a year of full-time salaries, and 30-minute shifts slot neatly around peak attendance from 210,000 visits [app]. Part-time cover keeps the pools staffed into busy sessions without exhausting the $900 recruitment budget [an]. However, part-time staff cannot open and close or complete gym induction checks properly [k], so the 14-hour day would still stretch the 40 existing full-time staff further, or require tighter supervision [app]. Four full-time lifeguards on $24,500 each would handle openings, closings and induction checks, with 5 weeks of leave rosterable around the summer peak [an]. Overall, the centre should hire the 4 full-time lifeguards because open/close and gym induction duties are essential to safe 14-hour days, and 8 part-timers would leave those duties uncovered [eval]. If attendances proved erratic after summer, some evening shifts could be converted to part-time once core full-time cover was secure [eval].

knowledge_max_2: Part-time: cheaper per hour, flexible, suits peaks
Full-time: committed, wider duties, end-to-end responsibility
application_max_2: $11.50 an hour vs $24,500 ($98,000 total); 210,000 visits; $900 budget
Open/close and gym induction duties; 5 weeks leave; 14-hour days; 2 pools
analysis_max_2: Cheaper flexible cover, but leaves opening/closing and induction uncovered
Full-time option guarantees daily end-to-end safety cover
evaluation_max_2: Clear recommendation justified by non-negotiable safety duties
Acknowledges replacing some shifts with part-time later if demand is volatile

scenario_stem:
Greenacres Garden Centre is a family-run business in Country X employing 22 permanent staff: 16 full-time and 6 part-time. It sells bedding plants, tools and garden furniture. Spring accounts for 60% of annual garden sales, with 1,800 plants sold per peak week at an average price of $9 across a 13-week season.

This year the owner needs 3 extra weekend assistants for March to May. She must choose how to advertise: $400 for a colour advert in the local newspaper, read mainly by residents over 55, or $150 online with younger, mobile-first reach but no guaranteed local targeting. The centre's last print advert, placed 2 years ago, generated 40 phone enquiries. The owner expects the online advert to attract younger applicants but fears fewer will be local. The recruitment budget is $600. Weekend assistants will help customers choose plants and load large purchases into cars.

questions.question_text: Identify two pieces of information a job advertisement could include.
questions.model_answer: A job advertisement could include the job title and key duties of the role, and the pay offered, working hours and how to apply. [2]

knowledge_max_2: Job title and key duties/responsibilities of the role
Pay offered, working hours, closing date or how to apply (any valid content)

questions.question_text: Explain two reasons why Greenacres Garden Centre should include clear details in its job advertisement for the 3 weekend assistants.
questions.model_answer: Clear details attract applicants who can actually do the job [k], so stating the 13-week March to May weekend pattern and duties such as helping customers and loading purchases filters out anyone wanting permanent, full-time work [app]. Precise details reduce wasted applications [k], meaning the $150 online or $400 print advert pulls in relevant candidates the first time rather than forcing a costly re-advertisement [app].

knowledge_max_2: Clear details attract suitable applicants and set realistic expectations
Clear details screen out unsuitable applicants, saving time and money
application_max_2: 13-week March to May weekend contract; 3 extra weekend assistants
$150 online vs $400 print choice; loading large purchases; plant sales at $9

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits of choosing the $150 online advert.
questions.model_answer: The online advert costs far less than print [k], saving $250 against the $400 newspaper advert and leaving $450 of the $600 budget for other recruitment tasks [app], which improves value for money across just 3 seasonal posts [an]. Online adverts also reach younger, mobile-first audiences quickly [k], going beyond the over 55 newspaper readership that dominated the last print campaign [app], which raises the chance of filling all 3 weekend roles before the 13-week season starts [an].

knowledge_max_2: Online advertising is cheaper than print
Online advertising reaches wider and younger audiences quickly
application_max_2: $150 online vs $400 print; save $250; $600 budget
Over 55 newspaper readership; 13 weeks; March to May
analysis_max_2: Savings improve cost-effectiveness and free budget for other hiring needs
Wider reach accelerates filling the 3 roles before the peak season

questions.question_text: Do you think Greenacres Garden Centre should place the $400 newspaper advert or the $150 online advert? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: The online advert is cheaper and reaches a broader, younger audience [k]. At $150 it leaves $450 of the $600 budget intact, and younger weekend applicants are more likely to be flexible, often browse mobile job sites and may know garden tools and tills, fitting a plant retail environment selling at an average of $9 [app]. Choosing online reduces cost per effective applicant and should fill the 3 roles before the 13 weeks begin [an]. However, the local newspaper is read mainly by residents over 55, who are the garden centre's core plant-buying customers and may be the most credible, knowledgeable weekend assistants [k]. The centre's last print advert generated 40 phone enquiries, proving its local pull, whereas the online advert offers no guaranteed local targeting [app]. Print might produce fewer but far better-suited local candidates, some with real horticultural knowledge for questions about 1,800 plants sold in a peak week [an]. Overall, the centre should place the online advert because it can be launched quickly, costs $250 less, and 3 seasonal roles can be filled from a wider pool without breaking the $600 budget [eval]. If the online response produces too few strong local candidates, a small print boost can follow, using the savings to reinforce the local message [eval].

scenario_stem:
Northgate Coach Travel is an intercity coach operator in Country X running 24 daily routes between 5 cities, employing 70 people. It has 44 full-time coach drivers on $34,000 a year and 26 office and depot staff.

The company has won an airport shuttle contract requiring 8 drivers within 8 weeks. The operations director must choose between two-round interviews (a 15-minute telephone screening followed by a 30-minute panel interview costing $140 per shortlisted candidate) or a single 20-minute informal chat with the owner, which is free. The contract requires drivers to hold a valid licence, a 5-year clean driving record and good customer-service skills. The interview budget is $1,400 and 40 drivers applied within 2 weeks. Round-one telephone screening at 15 minutes per candidate takes about 10 hours in total. Panel members include the operations director and the health and safety officer.

questions.question_text: Outline two advantages of using interviews to select candidates.
questions.model_answer: Interviews let the panel assess communication and customer-service skills face to face, and allow candidates to explain their 5-year clean driving record and route knowledge. [2]

Allows candidates to explain experience and driving history

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits of using two-round interviews to select the 8 airport drivers.
questions.model_answer: Telephone screening cheaply filters out unsuitable applicants [k], so the 15-minute first round can eliminate anyone lacking a valid licence or the 5-year clean record before staff time is spent, narrowing the 40 applicants to a serious shortlist [app]. Structured panel interviews give every shortlisted driver the same 30-minute question set [k], making customer-service answers directly comparable and enabling a fair choice of the strongest 8 within the $1,400 budget [app].

Structured interviews make assessments fair and comparable

questions.question_text: Explain two problems Northgate Coach Travel might face with a single informal chat.
questions.model_answer: Informal chats follow no fixed agenda [k], so each of the 40 applicants may be asked different questions and answers cannot be compared consistently when picking the 8 airport drivers [app], raising the risk of a biased or lucky selection for a safety-critical role [an]. A single chat also reveals little depth [k]. In 20 minutes the owner cannot verify driving records, licences or claim histories before trusting drivers with passengers on 24 daily routes [app], risking poor service that could damage, or even lose, the new airport contract [an].

questions.question_text: Do you think Northgate Coach Travel should use two-round interviews or a single informal chat to select the 8 airport drivers? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: Two-round interviews cost a little but are far more reliable [k]. The 15-minute telephone screening clears the 40 applicants cheaply, and the $1,400 budget covers panel interviews for up to 10 finalists at $140 each (10 x $140 = $1,400), selecting the strongest 8 on merit [app]. Structured, recorded answers protect the company from unfair-selection claims and let panel members probe customer-service skills properly [an]. However, the 20-minute informal chat is free, fast and might secure drivers within days, which helps if routes must start within 8 weeks [k]. For internal candidates from the 44 existing drivers it could work, but it cannot test new applicants consistently against licence and the 5-year clean-record requirement [app]. Saving $1,400 means little if an unfit driver causes an incident on the 24 daily routes [an]. Overall, the company should run two-round interviews because the airport contract demands verified records and strong customer-service skill, and the process fits the $1,400 budget exactly [eval]. The informal chat could follow the panel decision as a courtesy introduction, but never as the selection method [eval].

Informal chat: free, fast, but unstructured and unreliable for unknown applicants

scenario_stem:
The Reading Nook is an independent bookshop in Country X employing 7 staff: the owner, 2 full-time weekend managers on $21,500 a year, 3 part-time assistants on $9.50 an hour and 1 weekend cashier. Shop sales are $780,000 a year, with footfall peaking on Saturdays at 900 customers.

The owner must hire a replacement assistant and is writing the person specification. She is undecided between a strict specification requiring 2 years' retail experience and 5 school qualifications, or a flexible one accepting enthusiastic applicants without experience who love books and can work 12 Saturdays between March and May. Last year, 11 of 25 applicants met the strict criteria and the strict advert took 4 weeks to fill. Advertising that vacancy cost $240. Sales in April last year fell 8% because the shop was short-staffed on Saturdays. The owner wants candidates who will stay beyond the 12-Saturday season.

questions.question_text: Identify two qualities a person specification might include.
questions.model_answer: A person specification might include good communication and interpersonal skills, and relevant retail experience or availability on the required days. [2]

Relevant experience, qualifications or availability for the role

questions.model_answer: A person specification sets out exactly what the shop needs [k], so the owner can match candidates against a checklist instead of guessing; of the 25 applications last time, she could immediately set aside the 14 who lacked the 2 years' retail experience the shop wanted [app]. A clear specification makes shortlisting fair and consistent [k], so every applicant is judged against the same 5 school qualifications and the Saturday-availability requirement, reducing personal bias in a small independent team [app].

Only 11 of 25 applicants met it last year, and the strict advert took 4 weeks to fill at a cost of $240 in advertising [app]. If the same happens again, April's short-staffed dip, when sales fell 8%, could recur [an]. It also excludes enthusiastic, book-loving applicants [k], who could learn stock knowledge quickly and engage Saturday's 900 customers despite lacking 2 years' experience [app], narrowing the shop's personality and wasting free enthusiasm the community shop thrives on [an].

questions.question_text: Do you think The Reading Nook should use a strict person specification or a flexible one? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: A flexible specification widens the pool and speeds hiring [k]. Dropping the 2-years'-experience rule in favour of Saturday availability, enthusiasm for books and trainability suits $9.50-an-hour staff who can engage the 900 Saturday customers driving $780,000 of annual sales [app]. Faster hiring avoids another April dip like last year's 8% fall and saves a repeat of the $240 advertising outlay [an]. However, the strict specification with 2 years' experience and 5 school qualifications guarantees a baseline of competence, stock knowledge and dependable service [k]. If sales hinge on expert recommendations, an inexperienced hire might underperform and pile more work onto the 2 full-time weekend managers [app]. Strict criteria also cut the owner's workload by pre-filtering the 14 of 25 applicants who failed the requirements last time [an]. Overall, the owner should adopt the flexible specification with a short trial-shift assessment, because the 8% April sales drop showed the real cost of an empty seat and stock can be learned within a month in a bookshop [eval]. If the best applicants are inexperienced, she should choose the one who connects with customers and train them on stock in the first weeks [eval].

Strict spec guarantees baseline competence and reduces screening effort

scenario_stem:
Kestrel Security Services provides uniformed security officers for shopping centres, warehouses and office blocks in Country X, employing 120 officers. It has 80 full-time officers on $28,500 a year and 40 part-time evening officers. After winning 3 new contracts, the firm needs 10 more officers within 8 weeks.

The recruitment budget for advertising and interviews is $1,200. The operations manager wants to re-use last year's job description and person specification, but the new contracts require officers to patrol open car parks at night, operate radio equipment and complete incident reports, duties absent from the old documents. A fresh job analysis last time took 60 hours of staff time. Recruitment advertising costs $220 online and $500 in print. The firm received 75 enquiries from its last online advert. Officers receive 12 weeks of paid training after joining. The new contracts cover an additional 40 store locations.

questions.question_text: Define the term 'job analysis'.
questions.model_answer: Job analysis is the process of studying a job in detail to identify the tasks, duties and responsibilities involved and the skills and qualifications required to perform it. [2]

knowledge_max_2: Studying the job in detail: tasks, duties and responsibilities
Identifying the skills and qualifications needed to perform it

questions.question_text: Explain two benefits of carrying out a fresh job analysis before recruiting the 10 officers.
questions.model_answer: A job analysis reveals what the new contracts actually require [k]. The duties now include night car-park patrols, radio operation and incident reports, which are absent from the old documents, so the analysis defines the real job rather than a stale version [app]. It also produces an accurate job description and person specification [k], so the firm's 75 recent enquiries can be screened against the current demands before interviews are booked [app].

knowledge_max_2: Identifies the actual, current duties of the job
Forms the basis of an accurate job description and person specification

3 new contracts; 75 enquiries received; 10 officers needed within 8 weeks

questions.model_answer: The old job description omits the new night duties [k], so selected officers may arrive unprepared for car-park patrols, radios and incident reporting across the 3 new contracts and 40 additional locations [app], risking complaints, client dissatisfaction and even loss of the contracts [an]. Re-using stale documents also wastes advertising spend [k]. Money spent on the $220 online and $500 print adverts would attract applicants unsuitable for night patrols, forcing a re-advertisement within the 8-week window [app] and doubling selection costs beyond the $1,200 budget [an].

Attracts unsuitable applicants and wastes recruitment spend

questions.question_text: Do you think Kestrel Security Services should carry out a fresh job analysis or re-use last year's job description and person specification? Justify your answer.
questions.model_answer: A fresh job analysis is essential because the contracts changed [k]. The new duties (night car-park patrols, radio operation and incident reports across 3 contracts and 40 extra store locations) differ fundamentally from last year's role, so without analysis the job description would mislead both the 75 enquiries and the interview panel [app]. A small share of the $1,200 budget spent now prevents repeat hiring, client disputes and lost contracts later [an]. However, a fresh job analysis last time took 60 hours of staff time [k], time that could have covered billable patrols or officer training, and re-using old documents is free and fast [app]. If last year's specification were merely edited and re-published for $220 online, the 10 officers could be hired inside the 8-week window with minimal disruption [an]. Overall, the firm should carry out a fresh job analysis because the risk of appointing officers unsuited to night patrols and incident reporting far outweighs 60 staff-hours, and any cost gap can be closed by choosing the $220 online advert over print [eval]. Re-using old documents would be defensible only if the new contracts were identical to last year's, which they are not [eval].
